body:
Two gate test fixtures depend on ambient process state, so their outcome is decided by the machine rather than the code under test. Both are fixture defects; neither is a product defect. Fix both.

1. TIMESTAMP RACE (a real intermittent failure).
packages/prosecute/test/prosecute-tier-check-cli.test.mjs:594 'round-4 codex finding: a cross-author revision collision reports MISSING attestation, not truncation' fails on its own precondition (assert.equal(revA, revB)), not on the behaviour under test. A revision is `git-change:<baseSha>:<contentDigest>` (packages/core/lib/revision.mjs). scratchRepo() pins user.name, user.email and commit.gpgsign but commits with ambient dates, and a commit SHA hashes the author/committer timestamps at 1-second resolution. The two independently built repos therefore agree on the base SHA only when both baseline commits land inside the same wall-clock second. In observed failures the content digest matches and only the base SHA differs, which is the signature of exactly this race. Fix: pass GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE in the scratchRepo git helper's env so the collision the test asserts is constructed rather than accidental. Nothing in that file asserts two revisions DIFFER, so a fixed clock weakens no other case.

2. AMBIENT ENV LEAK (not intermittent; deterministic given an exported var).
scripts/test/rails-guard-bootstrap-ci.test.mjs builds throwaway repos and pins BASE_REF, but both scenario runners spawn the gate with `...process.env`. RAILS_BASE outranks BASE_REF in defaultBase() (packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/args.mjs), and RAILS_BASE is the documented manual escape hatch, so an operator who exports it to drive the gate by hand retargets every scenario at a branch the synthetic repo does not contain. Every failure surfaces as a bare exit 1 operational error with no hint the cause is environmental. Fix: spread a HERMETIC_ENV constant pinning RAILS_BASE (and, defensively, GITHUB_EVENT_PATH and ADLC_PR_REVIEWS, which are always set under GitHub Actions and flip readPrContext() away from the null a local run sees) ahead of each scenario's own env, so a test that deliberately supplies one still wins. This mirrors packages/rails-guard/test/ci-bin.test.mjs, which already pins RAILS_BASE/BASE_REF. No coverage is lost: RAILS_BASE resolution is owned by packages/rails-guard/test/ci-args.test.mjs, which injects env as an object literal and never reads process.env.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A 40-pair harness building two scratchRepo-shaped repos reports 0 base-SHA divergences with dates pinned (measured 15/40 divergent before the fix on a loaded machine).
   Verify: node --test packages/prosecute/test/prosecute-tier-check-cli.test.mjs run 10x consecutively, 0 failures (measured 1/10 failing before the fix).
2. The bootstrap suite passes identically with and without a leaked base ref.
   Verify: node --test scripts/test/rails-guard-bootstrap-ci.test.mjs AND RAILS_BASE=does-not-exist node --test scripts/test/rails-guard-bootstrap-ci.test.mjs both report 80 pass / 0 fail (measured 5 pass / 75 fail with the var set before the fix).
3. No product code changes; the diff touches only the two test files named in scope.
   Verify: git diff --stat lists exactly those two paths.
4. Full suite stays green.
   Verify: node scripts/run-tests.mjs reports all segments passed.
title: Make two gate test fixtures hermetic: pin scratch-repo commit dates and stop inheriting RAILS_BASE
